chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Sali, from Abu Al Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who marries a woman and stipulates to her that he will not take her out of her city, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He must fulfill that for her,' or he said: 'That is binding upon him.'
ai.seo_question: Is a husband legally bound to a stipulation in the marriage contract not to relocate his wife?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the binding nature of a specific marital stipulation preventing relocation, reflecting the Shia legal principle that agreed-upon conditions are enforceable unless they contradict the essence of marriage. This ruling underscores the importance of preserving the wife's social and familial stability, a key consideration in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital rights and obligations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Sali, from Abu Al Abbas,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who married the woman and he stipulated to her than he would not be taking her out from her city. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He has to fulfil with that to her’, or said: ‘That would be necessitated upon him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad and ‘Abd Allah sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa have narrated from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from abu al-‘Abbas who has said the following: “

About the case of a man who marries a woman with the condition that he will not take her out of her town, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He must keep that promise’ or that he (the Imam) said, ‘It is binding upon him.’”
